guide_title: Guide: descriptors, unicode-range and layout shift — fontstay.dev
guide_description: How metric-adjusted fallback fonts remove font-swap layout shift: the @font-face descriptors, browser support, unicode-range, Safari, formats, licenses and specifications.
credits_description: Data sources, tools and inspiration behind fontstay.dev, with their licenses.
credits_note: Sources, licenses and inspiration for the data and tools used here (English).
guide_intro: A short explanation of what the generated CSS does and why it prevents the text from jumping when your web font arrives.
guide_cls_text: While a web font loads, the browser draws the text in a fallback font. When the web font arrives the text is redrawn: if the glyphs are wider or the lines taller, lines wrap differently and everything below moves. Google measures this as Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS): 0.1 or less is good, above 0.25 is poor. Making the fallback font match the metrics of the web font keeps the lines where they are.
guide_descriptors_text: Each fallback is a local() system font declared with descriptors that rescale it: size-adjust scales the glyphs so the text has the same width, and ascent-override, descent-override and line-gap-override set the vertical metrics so the lines have the same height. The font-family stack lists the web font first, then the adjusted fallbacks, then a generic family.
guide_support_caption: First browser version that supports each feature (MDN browser-compat-data {version})
guide_support_note: — means not supported, ? means unknown. Browsers that lack a descriptor simply ignore it, so the CSS is safe everywhere.
guide_safari_text: Safari supports size-adjust (since 17) but not ascent-override, descent-override or line-gap-override. For those browsers the generator adds font-size-adjust, which matches the x-height of the web font, and a fixed line-height, which makes the line box independent of the fallback metrics.
guide_range_text: A face with a unicode-range is used only for the listed code points. Limiting the adjusted fallbacks to the characters the web font covers keeps the adjustment from applying to glyphs the web font will never draw. Ranges are compacted without loss (adjacent code points are merged) and match the subsets used by Google Fonts.
guide_formats_text: Use WOFF2 for the web: it is the smallest and every current browser supports it. WOFF, TrueType (TTF) and OpenType (OTF) files also work with @font-face. Font collections (TTC, OTC) cannot be used directly in a browser, so this tool splits them into separate fonts.
guide_licenses_text: A font file is software and its license decides whether you may put it on a website. The generated CSS only references fonts already installed on the visitor’s system (local()), but the web font you serve must be licensed for it:
guide_license_ofl: SIL Open Font License (OFL): free to use and embed, the font may not be sold on its own.
guide_license_apache: Apache License 2.0: free to use and embed with the license notice.
guide_license_ufl: Ubuntu Font Licence (UFL): free to use and embed, modified versions must be renamed.
guide_license_proprietary: Commercial and desktop licenses often do not cover web embedding: check for a separate web license.
guide_licenses_where: The license text and URL are in the font’s name table (name IDs 13 and 14) and the embedding permissions are in the OS/2 table (fsType). Always read the license from the font’s source as well.

mcp_title: MCP server for AI agents — fontstay.dev
mcp_description: Let an AI agent in your editor analyze local font files and write metric-adjusted fallback CSS: tools, setup for common MCP clients, example prompts and a sample result.
mcp_intro: The fontstay package includes a Model Context Protocol server. An AI agent in your editor can read your local font files, pick the fallback fonts for your audience and write the same fallback CSS as this app.
mcp_what_text: The server runs on your machine over stdio. It reads only the font files the agent names, writes nothing and makes no network requests. It is stateless: every call names its files and carries its own audience, so the agent can ask again with different options.
mcp_tools_text: The server exposes four read-only tools.
mcp_tool_analyze: Describes a font file: names, weight and style, detected type, vertical metrics, scripts, glyph count, variable axes, OpenType features and license.
mcp_tool_suggest: Lists the system font chosen as the fallback on each operating system, the audience share of each system and how much of the font’s glyph weight the fallbacks share with it.
mcp_tool_css: Generates the @font-face and font-family CSS, identical to the app and the command line.
mcp_tool_export: The same fit as CSS variables, Tailwind, Next.js, Nuxt, Astro, WordPress theme.json, Fontaine, preload tags or a loading script, with a suggested file name.
mcp_options_text: All tools except analyze_font take one to 16 font files (WOFF2, WOFF, TTF or OTF, up to 10 MB each) and the same options as the command line: audience (a Browserslist query), systems, locale, kind, unicode_range and scripts. Low glyph overlap and systems without fallback fonts come back as warnings after the result.
mcp_setup_text: Add the server to your MCP client. It starts with npx and needs Node.js 24.21 or newer.
mcp_setup_checkout: If the package is not on npm yet, build it in a checkout with pnpm cli:build and use node /path/to/packages/fontstay/dist/bin.js mcp as the command instead of npx. Relative font paths resolve against the directory the editor starts the server in.
mcp_prompts_text: Ask in plain language; the agent picks the tools.
mcp_prompt_1: Analyze fonts/Inter.woff2 and tell me which scripts it covers.
mcp_prompt_2: Write fallback CSS for fonts/Inter.woff2 for Windows and macOS users and add it to src/styles/fonts.css.
mcp_prompt_3: Generate the Tailwind theme for my Fira Sans files, then check the warnings.
mcp_sample_text: A get_css call for tests/fixtures/fonts/FiraSans-Regular.ttf, limited to Windows and macOS, without extra script faces.
mcp_limits_text: Bad input comes back as a tool error that the agent can read and correct.
mcp_limit_1: Audience queries that load a shared config or stats file (extends, in package) are rejected.
mcp_limit_2: Windows network paths (\\host\share) are not read.
mcp_limit_3: Layout shift needs a browser and is not available; use the app for it.
mcp_limit_4: The server speaks MCP protocol versions 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05, tools only.
mcp_cli_text: The same engine is available as a command line tool and a Node library in the fontstay package.
cli_description: Generate metric-adjusted fallback fonts in build pipelines and CI with the fontstay command-line tool and Node library.
cli_intro: The fontstay package is the fit engine of this site without the browser: a command-line tool and a Node library that read font files and print the same @font-face rules and exports as the app. It needs no DOM and makes no network requests, so it fits build pipelines and CI.
cli_install_text: The package is not published to npm yet. It requires Node 24 or newer; build it from a checkout of the repository. The examples below write fontstay for node packages/fontstay/dist/bin.js.
cli_commands_text: fit reads one or more font files (WOFF2, WOFF, TTF, OTF) and prints the fallback CSS. Several files are merged into one stylesheet, as in the app. mcp starts an MCP server on stdio for coding agents and takes no options.
cli_example_text: Fit a font for Windows and macOS without the Cyrillic and Greek faces. The output is the same text as the CSS export in the app.
cli_opt_systems: Systems to fit: windows, macos, ios, android, linux, chromeos. Default: every system with at least 1% share in the audience.
cli_opt_audience: Browserslist query, optionally with “os <system>” and “not os <system>” parts. Default: baseline widely available.
cli_opt_format: Output format, see below. Default: css.
cli_opt_kind: Generic family of the fallbacks: sans-serif, serif, monospace or cursive. Default: detected from the font.
cli_opt_locale: Frequency profile of the fit: en or ru. Default: en.
cli_opt_range: Add unicode-range with the glyphs each font covers.
cli_opt_scripts: Do not emit separate faces for Cyrillic and Greek.
cli_opt_out: Write the output to a file instead of stdout.
cli_opt_json: Print a JSON report instead of the file text.
cli_opt_help: Show the help or the version.
cli_formats_text: --format takes one of these values. They match the export formats of the app and start from the same fit.
cli_formats_example_text: Run this command for each format using the sample Fira Sans font. Output shown is from the built CLI.
cli_output_text: The file text goes to stdout. With --json the CLI prints a report instead, with the keys file (the output in the chosen format), fonts (family, detected kind, glyph coverage and the fallback picked per system for each font), shares (audience share of each system, in percent), systems, uncovered (systems in the audience without a fallback font) and audience (the resolved query and the number of matching browsers). The shares depend on the browser data at the time of the run.
cli_warnings_text: Warnings go to stderr, so they never end up in the output: a font whose fallbacks share less than 90% of its glyphs, and systems without any fallback font. With --out the CLI also reports the written file on stderr.
cli_library_text: fit takes font bytes and fitFiles reads files. Both return the CSS, the output in the requested format, a report per font and the audience shares. Failures throw FitRunError (invalid-audience, no-systems, no-fit) or FontParseError (for example invalid-font). The types are in index.d.ts.
cli_exit_1: Failure: a file that cannot be read, an invalid font, an invalid audience.
cli_exit_2: Usage error: an unknown command, no font file, an invalid option value.

ext_description: Bring the fonts of any website into fontstay.dev with the browser extension or the bookmarklet: what each one does, what it reads, and how to install it.
ext_intro: Both tools do the same job: they collect the fonts of the page you are looking at and open them in the generator, so you can build a fallback stack for a font that is not in the catalog. Nothing is uploaded: the data goes from that page's tab straight to a fontstay.dev tab in your browser.
ext_choose_bookmarklet: The bookmarklet works in every desktop browser and needs no installation, but a site with a strict Content Security Policy can block it (Firefox does so most often).
ext_choose_extension: The extension also works on sites with a strict Content Security Policy. For now it is installed from source in Chrome, Edge and other Chromium browsers.
ext_data_heading: What the tools read and send
ext_data_reads: When you run either tool on a page, it reads:
ext_data_item_page: The address of the site and the page title.
ext_data_item_fonts: The @font-face declarations of the page (family, weight, style, format, source URL), found in its style sheets.
ext_data_item_files: The font files the page uses, downloaded again by the page without cookies: at most 8 files, 10 MB each and 30 MB in total.
ext_data_item_styles: The family, size, weight and line height that the body, the first headings and the first button use.
ext_data_not_read: They do not read the text of the page, forms, cookies or storage.
ext_data_no_upload: Nothing is uploaded to a server. The data is passed to a fontstay.dev tab in your browser, checked and stored in your browser for ten minutes at most.
ext_data_confirm: The generator shows a summary ("Import from <site>?") and uses nothing until you accept it.
ext_bookmarklet_text: A bookmarklet is a bookmark that holds a small program instead of an address. Clicking it on a page runs the program on that page.
ext_bookmarklet_step_drag: Drag the "Send to fontstay" link below to your bookmarks bar. If you cannot drag it, copy the code, create a new bookmark and paste the code as its address.
ext_bookmarklet_step_open: Open the website whose fonts you want.
ext_bookmarklet_step_click: Click the bookmark. A fontstay.dev tab opens and asks you to confirm the import.
ext_bookmarklet_manual: If the browser blocks the new tab, the bookmarklet copies the font names, sizes and the page title (no font files) to the clipboard. Paste them into the "Add a font" field of the generator; the origin is then shown as unverified.
ext_bookmarklet_csp: If the site blocks the bookmarklet, use the extension or paste the copied data into the "Add a font" field.
ext_extension_text: The extension adds a toolbar button. Click it on any page and a fontstay.dev tab opens with the fonts of that page, ready to confirm.
ext_extension_permissions: It asks for the "activeTab" and "scripting" permissions only. It cannot read any page until you click its button, and its only standing access to a site is the fontstay.dev import page.
ext_extension_chromium: Chrome, Edge and other Chromium browsers (Manifest V3): install from source, see below.
ext_extension_stores: Browser stores: the extension is not published in the Chrome Web Store, Edge Add-ons or Firefox Add-ons yet. Store links will appear here when it is.
ext_extension_step_download: Download the repository from GitHub (the green Code button, then Download ZIP) and unzip it, or clone it with git.
ext_extension_step_developer: Open chrome://extensions (edge://extensions in Edge) and turn on Developer mode.
ext_extension_step_load: Choose Load unpacked and select the "extension" folder of the repository.
ext_extension_step_use: Open a website and click the fontstay button in the toolbar (pin it from the puzzle-piece menu if it is hidden).
share_dialog_empty: Nothing but the defaults would be stored in the link.
share_dialog_too_long: The link is very long and may not open in every browser or messenger.
share_part_panel: Open panel, system and font face
share_part_preview: Preview settings, mode and device width
share_part_site_fonts: Heading and body fonts of the imported site
